title: What pattern do digital roots follow when we add the same number?
description: The digital roots of the multiples of four from four to thirty six, and of seven, thirteen, nineteen, twenty five and thirty one, move round a ring of nine. Keeko's doubt is that the digital root of twenty eight is ten.
teaching_notes: One idea: adding the same number each time moves the digital root by a fixed step round the ring of one to nine. Watch for students who write a digital root of ten or more instead of adding the digits again.

source: Write the digital roots of the consecutive multiples of 4 from 4 to 36, and of the numbers 7, 13, 19, 25, 31, which are 1 more than multiples of 6
video_script.why: A learner sees that adding the same number each time moves the digital root by a fixed step round the ring of nine.
video_script.substitution: the book's own lists, the multiples of 4 from 4 to 36 and the numbers 7, 13, 19, 25, 31
video_script.anchor: a ring of the nine digital roots with the roots of the two lists marked on it
video_script.wrong_answer: the digital root of twenty eight is ten
video_script.wrong_move: adds the digits once and writes a two digit sum as the root
video_script.payoff_line: Multiples of four go through all nine roots. Numbers one more than a multiple of six repeat seven, four and one.

final_answer.value: Multiples of 4 cycle through all nine roots; numbers 1 more than multiples of 6 cycle 7, 4, 1
final_answer.spoken: multiples of four go through all nine roots, and numbers one more than a multiple of six repeat seven, four and one

hold_back: Multiples of 4 cycle through all nine roots; numbers 1 more than multiples of 6 cycle 7, 4, 1
maths_rules: each step adds 4 to the root, taking away 9 when it passes 9: 8 + 4 = 12, 12 - 9 = 3
the next multiple, 40, has root 4, so the roots repeat after nine steps and all nine appear once
adding 6 is the same as taking away 3 from the root, because 6 = 9 - 3; from 1, add 9 to make 10, then take away 3 to get 7
video_script.design: One idea: a fixed step moves the digital root round a ring of nine. Assumes the digital root and the digit sum. The ring of nine roots stays on the board all video.

beats.on_screen: title card Digital roots in a pattern; the multiples of 4 from 4 to 36 in a row, and below them 7, 13, 19, 25, 31, with a question mark

marks.scene: the title card arrives and the multiples of 4 are written in a row
marks.ask: the numbers 7, 13, 19, 25, 31 appear below and the question mark appears

narration: <bookmark mark='scene'/>This is a question from your book about digital roots. First come the multiples of four in a row, from four to thirty six.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>It also asks about seven, thirteen, nineteen, twenty five and thirty one. Each is one more than a multiple of six.
What pattern do the digital roots make?

beats.on_screen: the two lists stay on the board while the child thinks

marks.think: Keeko sits at the corner of the board

narration: <bookmark mark='think'/>Think and tell.

beats.on_screen: a ring of the nine digital roots 1 to 9 with an arrow that goes round and back to 1 after 9

marks.ring: the ring of the nine roots appears
marks.round: an arrow goes from 9 back to 1 round the ring

narration: <bookmark mark='ring'/>The digital roots one to nine sit on a ring.
<bookmark mark='round'/>After nine we come back to one. Taking away nine from a number above nine brings it back onto the ring.

beats.on_screen: Given: multiples of 4 from 4 to 36; the numbers 7, 13, 19, 25, 31
narration: <bookmark mark='given'/>Given, the multiples of four from four to thirty six. Also the numbers seven, thirteen, nineteen, twenty five and thirty one.

beats.on_screen: To find: the digital root of every number in both lists, and the pattern

marks.find: the question is written under the given line

narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to find the digital root of every number, and the pattern they make.

marks.start: 4 and 8 are written with roots 4 and 8
marks.all: the nine roots 4, 8, 3, 7, 2, 6, 1, 5, 9 are written under the nine multiples

narration: <bookmark mark='start'/>Step one, four has digital root four, and eight has digital root eight.
<bookmark mark='add'/>Each step adds four to the root. Eight plus four is twelve, and taking away nine leaves three.
<bookmark mark='all'/>The roots are four, eight, three, seven, two, six, one, five and nine.

beats.on_screen: The next multiple, 40, has root 4 again. All nine roots appear once before the pattern repeats

marks.nine: the nine roots are ticked on the ring

narration: <bookmark mark='forty'/>Step two, the next multiple is forty, and its digital root is four again.
<bookmark mark='nine'/>All nine roots appear once before the pattern repeats.

beats.on_screen: 7, 13, 19, 25, 31 have roots 7, 4, 1, 7, 4. Adding 6 is the same as taking away 3 from the root, because 6 = 9 - 3

marks.roots: the roots 7, 4, 1, 7, 4 are written under the numbers
marks.six: an arrow marked plus 6 is changed to minus 3
marks.wrap: from 1, add 9 to make 10, then take away 3 to get 7 is written

narration: <bookmark mark='roots'/>Step three, look at seven, thirteen, nineteen, twenty five and thirty one. Their roots are seven, four, one, seven and four.
<bookmark mark='six'/>Adding six is the same as taking away three from the root, because six is nine less three.
<bookmark mark='wrap'/>From one we add nine to make ten, then take away three to get seven.

marks.match: the root 1 is ticked in the list

narration: <bookmark mark='sum'/>Step four, check twenty eight. Two plus eight is ten, and one plus zero is one.
<bookmark mark='match'/>That matches the root one in our list.

beats.on_screen: Answer: Multiples of 4 cycle through all nine roots; numbers 1 more than multiples of 6 cycle 7, 4, 1
narration: <bookmark mark='ans'/>Multiples of four go through all nine roots. Numbers one more than a multiple of six repeat seven, four and one.

beats.on_screen: Keeko with a raised hand beside the number 28
narration: <bookmark mark='hand'/>Keeko has raised a hand. Let us check the doubt and solve it.

beats.on_screen: Keeko's bubble shows 2 + 8 = 10, root 10; then 1 + 0 = 1 appears; the bubble is struck through
narration: <bookmark mark='doubt'/>Keeko thinks the digital root of twenty eight is ten.
<bookmark mark='again'/>But ten still has two digits. Add them again, and one plus zero is one.
<bookmark mark='fix'/>A digital root always has a single digit, from one to nine.
